title: Recovery of compatible original levels from a torsion-controlled second-ideal triple
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian, $I,K$ quasi-coherent ideals, $M\in\operatorname{Coh}(X,I)$, and $H$ coherent, as in [pqf-def-locnoeth], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Suppose $\alpha:M\to\widehat H_I$ has component kernels and cokernels killed by one positive power of $K$. Let $N\in\operatorname{Coh}(X,K)$, $\delta:N\to\widehat H_K$, and an isomorphism of double diagrams $\sigma_{e,n}:N_e/I^nN_e\simeq M_n/K^eM_n$ be given. Let $\theta_{e,n}:(H/K^eH)/I^n\simeq(H/I^nH)/K^e$ be the quotient interchange characterized by the projections from $H$, and assume the comparison square with $\alpha_n$ and $\delta_e$ commutes. Let $F$ be coherent, $a:F\to H$ have actual kernel and cokernel killed by one positive power of $K$, and $\beta:N\simeq\widehat F_K$ satisfy $\delta=\widehat a_K\circ\beta$. Then there exist isomorphisms $\varphi_n:F/I^nF\simeq M_n$ for all positive $n$, compatible with every transition of the I-adic diagrams.

proof.text: Construct Xi, the natural completed comparison of the original I-levels, by commuting the two quotient operations and using sigma, theta, beta and the comparison square.

At each I-level, the reduced map a has K^(2s)-torsion kernel and cokernel. Completing alpha_n gives uniform K^(2t)-torsion components. Apply the existing torsion-triple theorem to this completed map, and compare its selected triple with both supplied coherent triples. Compose the inverse of the first comparison isomorphism with the second to get phi_n; cancel the two comparison isomorphisms to prove that phi_n respects both the map to H/I^nH and Xi.

For any transition, the composites have equal maps to H/I^mH by naturality of alpha and reduced a, and equal completions by naturality of Xi. The target comparison alpha_m has a power-torsion kernel, so completion together with that comparison detects the composites. Forget the coherent subcategory to obtain the required natural family of ambient module isomorphisms.
